summary: SSO login bounce for internal analytics after ingress path-rewrite rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Internal users in the Data/Analytics org are experiencing an SSO "login bounce" (redirect loop) when attempting to sign in to the analytics console. The loop began shortly after an ingress/edge-proxy path-rewrite change was rolled out.

Impact:
- Internal analytics dashboard access disrupted for ~12 users during morning reports.
- Affects internal productivity; not customer-facing but blocks critical internal workflows.

Environment:
- prod | us-west
- Affected service: analytics.console.redwood.ai (behind edge-proxy / ingress v2.4.0)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Navigate to https://analytics.console.redwood.ai
2) Click "Sign in with SSO"
3) Observe redirect to IdP and back to console; browser lands on /sso/callback then immediately redirects to IdP again (302 loop).

Observed behavior:
- Browser sequence: GET / -> 302 to IdP -> POST SAML -> 302 to /sso/callback -> 302 back to IdP -> repeat.
- SAML assertion appears valid in IdP logs; session cookie is issued but console does not accept it due to path mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- Single POST SAML flow ending in a 200/302 into authenticated console session, not a redirect loop.

Relevant logs and traces are attached in logs field and referenced in investigation notes below.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Open private/incognito browser to rule out stale cookies.
2) Visit analytics.console.redwood.ai and initiate SSO.
3) Capture network waterfall and follow redirect chain; verify final redirect target and cookie path.
4) Check ingress access logs for trace id and compare to IdP assertion RelayState.
logs: 2024-11-02T09:50:12Z ingress-proxy ERROR rewrite: strip_prefix removed trailing slash from /sso/callback/ -> /sso/callback (trace=xyz123)
2024-11-02T09:50:12Z console WARN sso: RelayState mismatch: expected '/sso/callback/' got '/sso/callback' (trace=xyz123)
2024-11-02T09:50:12Z idp INFO saml: assertion validated for user=ajones@redwood.ai RelayState='/sso/callback/' (request=abc789)
investigation_notes: 09:55 - Correlated increase in 302->GET redirect loops in ingress access logs starting at 2024-11-02 09:48 UTC, coincident with edge-proxy v2.4.0 rollout.
09:58 - IdP confirms SAML responses were issued successfully; assertion audience and signatures valid. RelayState carried trailing slash '/sso/callback/' in IdP logs.

10:05 - ingress-proxy path_rewrite rule strips trailing slashes for normalized routing; this turns '/sso/callback/' into '/sso/callback' which the console SSO handler treats as a different path and rejects the session restore, causing redirect back to IdP.

10:12 - Session cookie issued with path '/sso/callback/' by console; because the request landed at '/sso/callback' the cookie was not matched by the browser, leading to a missing session and redirect loop.
10:30 - Reproduced locally in staging by toggling strip_trailing_slash flag in ingress; confirmed same redirect loop behavior.

Hypothesis: ingress path normalization introduced by edge-proxy v2.4.0 created a mismatch between IdP RelayState/ACS and console's expected callback path, resulting in session not being established despite successful SAML assertion.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied 2024-11-02 12:03 UTC: reverted ingress/edge-proxy v2.4.0 path_rewrite change which immediately stopped redirect loops for affected users.
Longer-term fix: 1) Patch edge-proxy to preserve trailing slash for SSO callback paths (PR #942). 2) Harden console SSO handler to accept normalized ACS URIs with or without trailing slash. 3) Add synthetic SSO login test in CI that asserts successful end-to-end login post-rollout.
Follow-up: coordinate with IdP team to ensure ACS normalization contract and update runbook to include SSO smoke test as part of ingress rollouts.
resolution: Workaround applied; permanent patch in review
notes: Impacted group: Data/Analytics internal users; ~12 confirmed reports during morning window.
Not customer-facing but high internal priority during reporting hours.
Postmortem scheduled to capture rollout testing gaps and update runbooks.
